title: Amphibian room — White’s tree frogs: excessive shedding and sudden deaths
presentation: A private collection of twenty amphibians. Five White’s tree frogs are shedding excessively, sitting with limbs splayed and reddened ventral skin, and three have died within a week of new frogs arriving from an online seller.

stages.title: Assess the collection
stages.briefing: Affected frogs: excessive skin sloughing, ventral and thigh erythema, abnormal posture with hind limbs splayed, loss of righting reflex in two, inappetence. Three deaths in a week. New arrivals introduced without quarantine ten days before signs began. Room temperature 24°C, water dechlorinated, enclosures cleaned with a shared sponge and shared water containers.
stages.prompt: Which findings point to a transmissible skin disease?

options.label: Excessive sloughing with ventral erythema across several frogs
options.detail: Skin as the primary organ affected

options.label: Loss of righting reflex before death
options.detail: Electrolyte failure across damaged skin

options.label: Signs beginning ten days after unquarantined arrivals
options.detail: Introduction of an agent

options.label: Shared sponge and water containers
options.detail: The route between enclosures — husbandry, not a clinical sign

options.label: Room temperature 24°C
options.detail: Within a tolerable range for the species

stages.explanation: Amphibian skin is a respiratory and osmoregulatory organ, so a disease that damages it kills by electrolyte failure — which is exactly what the lost righting reflex represents. Sloughing with ventral erythema across several animals ten days after unquarantined arrivals is chytridiomycosis until excluded, and the shared cleaning equipment explains how it moved.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: You can swab live frogs and submit the dead ones.

options.label: Skin swabs of ventral surfaces and toe webbing for Batrachochytrium qPCR
options.detail: The reference test, and it distinguishes Bd from Bsal

options.label: Wet mount of shed skin for zoosporangia
options.detail: Immediate, if you know what to look for

options.label: Post-mortem with histopathology of skin
options.detail: Intracellular zoosporangia within hyperkeratotic epidermis

options.label: Ranavirus PCR on tissues
options.detail: The other cause of mass amphibian mortality

options.label: Bacterial culture from skin and coelom
options.detail: Secondary sepsis, common and treatable

options.label: Serum biochemistry on affected frogs
options.detail: Sample volume is prohibitive and it will not change the diagnosis

options.label: Faecal flotation as the primary test
options.detail: Endoparasites do not cause epidermal sloughing and death

stages.explanation: The swab qPCR is what makes this diagnosis, and swabbing the right places — ventrum and toe webbing, where the fungus concentrates — is the technique that decides whether it works. Running ranavirus in parallel is standard practice because the two present identically and only one is treatable, and treating the wrong one costs a collection.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis qPCR strongly positive in four of five affected frogs and in two of the new arrivals with no clinical signs; Bsal negative. Wet mount: zoosporangia visible in shed skin. Histopathology: epidermal hyperkeratosis with intracellular zoosporangia. Ranavirus PCR negative. Skin culture: mixed Gram-negatives including Aeromonas. Electrolytes on one frog: sodium and potassium both low.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Chytridiomycosis from Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis
options.detail: qPCR, wet mount and histology all agree

options.label: The new arrivals introduced it and are subclinical carriers
options.detail: Two positive frogs with no signs

options.label: Electrolyte loss across damaged skin is the mechanism of death
options.detail: Low sodium and potassium with loss of righting reflex

options.label: Secondary bacterial infection is present
options.detail: Aeromonas cultured from damaged skin

options.label: Ranavirus is the cause of the deaths
options.detail: PCR negative

options.label: Bsal is present and the collection is a Bsal risk
options.detail: Bsal specifically negative

stages.explanation: Distinguishing Bd from Bsal and from ranavirus is the whole point of the panel: Bd is treatable with itraconazole baths and temperature management, ranavirus is not, and Bsal carries different legal and biosecurity obligations. The low electrolytes explain the deaths mechanistically, which is why supportive electrolyte therapy sits alongside the antifungal.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Bd qPCR positive in affected frogs and in two symptom-free new arrivals, zoosporangia on wet mount and histology, Bsal and ranavirus negative, secondary Aeromonas, low sodium and potassium.

options.label: Chytridiomycosis (B. dendrobatidis) introduced by unquarantined arrivals, with secondary bacterial infection
options.detail: Confirmed agent, route of entry and complication

options.label: Ranavirus infection
options.detail: PCR negative

options.label: Bsal infection
options.detail: Specifically negative

options.label: Primary bacterial dermatosepticaemia
options.detail: Secondary to the fungal skin damage

options.label: Husbandry-related dysecdysis
options.detail: Does not explain positive qPCR, zoosporangia or three deaths

stages.explanation: This diagnosis is as much a biosecurity finding as a clinical one: itraconazole bathing with electrolyte support and raised temperature for affected frogs, treatment of the subclinical carriers, disinfection that kills zoospores, an end to shared sponges, and a real quarantine protocol. Bd released into native amphibian populations is a conservation problem, so the advice extends beyond the collection.
